questions.question: What is a database index primarily used for?
options: Encrypting data so it can't be read by unauthorized users
Letting a database find matching rows quickly instead of scanning every row in a table
Making a table use less disk space
Automatically backing up the entire database
questions.explanation: An index is a separate, sorted structure that lets the database jump directly to matching rows, similar to a book's index letting you jump to a page instead of reading cover to cover.

questions.question: Why do AI/RAG systems typically use a vector database in addition to a relational database?
options: Vector databases are always faster for everything
Vector databases store embeddings and are optimized for finding content with similar meaning, which relational databases aren't designed for
Relational databases can't store any text data
Vector databases replace the need for any other storage
questions.explanation: Vector databases store embeddings (numeric representations of meaning) and are optimized for similarity search, a fundamentally different query pattern than the exact-match/structured queries relational databases excel at.

questions.question: A chat history feature takes 8 seconds to load once a user has 10,000 messages. Which question best identifies a likely, well-understood root cause?
options: Should we just tell users to have fewer conversations?
Is the lookup filtering or sorting on a field (like the user or the creation time) that is missing a database index?
Can we switch to a completely different programming language?
Why do we store chat history at all?
questions.explanation: A missing index on a frequently filtered or sorted column is one of the most common, well-understood causes of a query slowing down significantly as a table grows.
